question.leadin: This empire engaged in ritualized "flower wars" with its neighbors.
question.text: Identify this Mesoamerican empire whose capital was Tenochtitlan. They were defeated by Hernan Cortez.
question.clue: The Stone of Tizoc was created by people in this empire, which achieved huge agricultural output by building artificial islands on swamps to create so-called "floating gardens" or chinampas.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about Mesoamerican civilizations.
swap.text: This civilization on the Yucatan had a number system based on twenty and a calendar known as the Long Count that some interpreted to predict that the world would end in the year 2012. It should be noted that the world has failed to do so.
swap.clue: The Temple of Inscriptions houses anajaw("ah-how")from this civilizationknown as Pacal the Great who reigned for 68 years in its city-state of Palenque("pah-LEN-kay").

question.text: This Mesoamerican culture played the ballgame in remembrance of the mythical Hero Twins, who played it to escape Xibalba ("shee-BAL-bah"). Thirteen ballcourts were built by this culture at its site of Chichen Itza on the Yucatan Peninsula.
question.clue: A revolt of these people began a fifty-year long Caste War in the second half of the 19th century.

swap.leadin: They were centered at sites such as Tres Zapotes, San Lorenzo, and La Venta.
swap.text: Identify this earliest Meso-American civilization centered in Mexico, famous for its large stone heads.
swap.clue: This culture created "elongated man" figurines as well as a greenstone statue of a man holding a were-jaguar ("wair-jaguar").

question.text: Under the direction of Enrico Martinez, the Spanish conquerors of Tenochtitlan drained this body of water upon which the city was built.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about pyramids around the world.
swap.text: The Pyramid of the Sun at this famed Mesoamerican site is the third largest pyramid in the world. Home to the Avenue of the Dead and the Pyramid of the Moon, the mysterious inhabitants of this ancient city were also known for the export of obsidian.
swap.clue: The decline of this city has been attributed to an increase in power of the "intermediate elites" by archaeologists such as Linda Manzanilla.

question.text: Moctezuma was imprisoned by Hernan Cortes, who left this conquistador as acting commander while he confronted a hostile expedition led by Panfilo de Narvaez ("PON-fee-loh day nar-VYE-ezz"). This conquistador later ordered the Massacre in the Great Temple.
question.clue: The revolt was set off by a massacre of Aztec nobles engineered by this officer, who tried to claim Quito, but was paid off by forces under Francisco Pizarro.

swap.leadin: This group is divided between "highland" and "lowland" cultures, such as the Yucatec.
swap.text: Name this people group that named an ancient Mesoamerican civilization of city-states in and around modern-day Guatemala. The city of Chichen Itza was built by this people group.
swap.clue: A leader of these people named Pacal the Great ruled Palenque ("PAH-len-kay"), which was abandoned during their supposed 9th-century collapse.

question.leadin: Camilla Townsend used only texts in this language to write her "New History," Fifth Sun.
question.text: Name this language used in the right columns of the Florentine Codex, where it parallels a translation of the same text in a European language.
question.clue: Historians learned to write in this language at schools called calmecacs ("kahl-MAY-kahks").

swap.text: Seventh century CE rulers of this city adopted the title of "ball player" when they took the throne of this Maya city in modern-day Chiapas.
swap.clue: The French explorer Jean-Frederic Waldeck resided for a time at this city, where a leafy corn plant mural is located at its "foliated cross" complex.

question.leadin: The story of the maiden Theodora and other cultural histories of these people appear in the books of Chilam Balam.
question.text: Name these people who fought the Caste War for greater autonomy over the Yucatan peninsula. These people abandoned the city of Chichen Itza during their postclassical period.
question.clue: King Pacal of these people was born on 9.8.9.13.0 in this people's "Long Count" calendar.

swap.leadin: Major wars between polities of this civilization were recorded with glyphs depicting stars, causing them to be dubbed "star wars."
swap.text: Name this ancient Mesoamerican civilization whose people built cities such as Tikal and Chichen Itza.
swap.clue: The Izapan culture was a major predecessor to this civilization, which was not conquered by the Spanish until 1541 by Pedro de Alvarado.

question.leadin: A series of figures constructed by this civilization were unearthed by Matthew and Marion Stirling.
question.text: Name this civilization whose art frequently featured the were-jaguar motif. Colossal stone heads constructed by this civilization were found at sites such as San Lorenzo and La Venta.
question.clue: Much of their art is based on a jaguar god, including much in that capital, La Venta.

swap.leadin: One artifact from this civilisation was a jade mosaic mask of a "bat god"
swap.text: Identify this pre-Columbian civilisation which had its capital at Monte Alban. The first known artifact that includes this civilisation's writing is a danzante ("dahn-SAHN-tay") stone depicting a dead and bloodied man strung upside-down.
swap.clue: The golaba, bigana and coqui("KO-kee") were officials in this civilization, whose site of Lambityeco ("lam-bee-tee-ECK-oh") is home to depictions of its chief lightning god.

question.leadin: This figure reconquered Cozumel, following the failed attempt a year earlier by Juan de Grijalva and this figure's manipulation of the visit of five tax collectors to Zempoala set the tone for his greatest conquest.
question.text: Name this figure who won the Battle of Otumba against disorganized natives, after his lieutenant, Pedro de Alvarado, had thousands of nobles killed for worshipping Huitzilopochtli during the Toxcatl Massacre.
question.clue: The Florentine Codex details how this man's subordinate, Pedro de Alvarado, massacred most of the people at a festival in the Templo Mayor, leading to the retaliatory murder of this man's soldiers during La Noche Triste.

swap.text: Even earlier than in India, the Mayans used a seashell to represent zero on this calendar system, which divides time into units such as baktun and katun.

question.leadin: Misinterpretation of this system's transition to b'aktun 13.0.0.0 resulted in incorrect predictions by many that the world would end on December 21, 2012.
question.text: Name this timekeeping system, whose 365-day long Haab approximated the solar year even more accurately than a Gregorian counterpart in Western Europe.
question.answerHtml: Mayan calendar [anti-prompt on specific Mayan calendars or “Long Count calendar”; prompt on Mesoamerican calendars or generic things]
question.clue: The Book of Chilam Balam of Chumayel discusses this system, which was split into the divine Tzolk'in and civil Haab' derived from "Venus rounds."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the 378 CE coup d'etat against King Jaguar Paw.
swap.text: In another military intervention almost a millennium later, Chichen Itza dispatched mercenaries to force nearby city-states to join this league, which united most Mayan city-states until its namesake city was destroyed around 1400.

question.leadin: Gardens in this city could only be reached by a flight of 520 marble steps, which referenced the highly significant number of 52 for the people who lived here.
question.text: What city-state, which was founded in the 12th century, was the second most important member of a Triple Alliance whose least important member was the late-to-join Tlacopan?
question.clue: This city, likely founded by the Chichimecs, became the capital of the Acolhua after they moved from Coat-linchan.

swap.leadin: Unlike its rival, this Mayan city had a line of female rulers within its "Kaan dynasty," a name that refers to its glyph emblem of a snake head.
swap.text: Name this Snake Kingdom known for being the bitter enemy of Tikal during the Classical Mayan period.
swap.clue: This city whose ruler Sky Witness achieved a major power reversal by converting Caracol from a vassal of this city's rival Tikal into an ally. Today, this city is identified as the capital of the "Kingdom of the Snake."
